items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about tide pools:

'Tide pools are found on rocky shores where ocean water collects when the tide goes out. Inside a tide pool you might see sea stars, anemones, hermit crabs, and small fish. The animals have to survive both underwater and exposed to air and sun when the tide is low.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a close-up photograph of an actual tide pool, taken from above, showing the rocky pool of water with several of the animals mentioned (sea star, anemone, hermit crab) visible inside it. This would help because the paragraph describes what is inside a tide pool, and seeing the animals in their real environment would make the description concrete for listeners who have never seen one. A labeled version with arrows pointing to each animal would be even more helpful.

steps: The paragraph describes what tide pools are and what lives inside them.
The listener needs to see what these animals look like in a tide pool — many second graders have never seen one.
A photograph from above showing the pool with sea star, anemone, hermit crab, and small fish makes the description real.
Adding labels helps listeners connect the visual to the names in the description.
A photograph of the ocean or of individual animals in a tank would not show the specific tide pool environment.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about her daily school schedule:

'Every morning we start with reading at 8:30. Then at 9:15 we switch to math. At 10:30 we have a break, and when we come back at 10:45 we do writing. Lunch is at noon, and in the afternoon we have science, social studies, and specials.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a daily schedule chart with two columns: one for the time and one for the subject. It should list each block in order from 8:30 to the end of the afternoon, with the subject name next to each time. This helps listeners follow along and remember the order of events. A clock image beside each time would make it even easier for second graders who are still learning to read a clock.

steps: The paragraph describes a sequence of events with specific times.
Listeners cannot hold all those times and subjects in memory from hearing them once.
A two-column chart (time | subject) shows the sequence clearly and lets listeners check back.
Adding a clock image beside each time supports students who are still learning clock-reading.
A photograph of a classroom would not show the schedule; a chart is needed.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about how light passes through a prism:

'When white light enters a prism, it slows down and bends. Different colors of light bend by different amounts, so they separate from each other. Red bends the least and violet bends the most. When they come out the other side, they form a rainbow of colors in order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a diagram showing a beam of white light entering a triangular prism on one side, and on the other side the separated colors spreading out in order: red at one edge, then orange, yellow, green, blue, and violet at the other edge. Arrows should show the direction of the light, and each color should be drawn in its actual color. This directly shows the invisible bending process and the rainbow order that words alone are hard to picture.

steps: The paragraph describes an invisible process: light bending differently by color inside a prism.
A diagram of a prism with white light entering and colored rays spreading out on the other side makes the invisible process visible.
The colors should be drawn in order and in their actual colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet.
Arrows show the direction of the light and suggest the bending.
A photograph of a rainbow would show the result but not how or why it happens.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph recounting the experience of moving to a new school:

'My first week at Riverside Elementary was confusing because the building is shaped like a U and I kept walking in circles. The cafeteria is at the bottom of the U, the gym is on the left side, and the second-grade classrooms are at the top right. I got lost going from the gym to my classroom three times.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a simple top-down map of the school building showing its U shape. The cafeteria should be labeled at the bottom, the gym on the left side, and the second-grade classrooms at the top right. A dotted line could trace the route from the gym to the classroom to help listeners understand why the student kept getting lost. This visual directly supports the spatial description and makes the confusing layout easy to see.

steps: The paragraph is about a spatial layout: a U-shaped building with three key locations.
A top-down map of the U-shaped school with labeled locations shows the layout clearly.
Adding a dotted line from the gym to the classroom shows the confusing route.
This visual makes the source of the confusion understandable — walking in a U is disorienting.
A photograph of a school from outside would not show the interior layout.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about how seeds travel:

'Seeds travel in many ways. Some seeds, like dandelions, have fluffy parts that let the wind carry them. Others, like burrs, have hooks that catch on animal fur. Coconuts float on the ocean to reach new shores. Some seeds are inside fruit, and when animals eat the fruit, they drop the seeds somewhere new.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a four-panel diagram, with one panel for each type of seed travel: wind (dandelion with arrows showing wind direction), animal (burr stuck to animal fur), water (coconut floating), and animals eating fruit (an animal dropping a seed). Each panel should label the method. This directly matches the paragraph's structure of four examples and lets listeners see each type as it is described.

steps: The paragraph describes four different methods seeds use to travel.
A four-panel diagram with one method per panel matches the paragraph's structure.
Each panel should show the seed and an arrow or image showing the method: wind, hooks on fur, floating, eaten and dropped.
Labels connect each image to the method name.
A single photograph of a dandelion would show only one of the four methods.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about her experience watching a solar eclipse:

'We used special glasses to watch the eclipse. First the moon started to cover one edge of the sun. Slowly more and more of the sun was covered. Then for about two minutes, the sun was completely blocked and the sky around us turned dark. Finally the sun came back.

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a sequence of five images showing the sun at each stage: (1) full sun, (2) moon beginning to cover one edge, (3) sun half covered, (4) sun completely blocked (total eclipse, dark ring visible), (5) sun returning. Each image should be labeled with the stage. This matches the paragraph's description of a process that happened step by step, and it shows something that is very hard to picture from words alone.

steps: The paragraph describes a process with five stages: full sun, partial coverage beginning, more coverage, total block, sun returning.
A five-panel sequence diagram shows each stage visually.
Each panel should show what the sun looked like at that stage.
Labels like 'Stage 1,' 'Stage 2' etc. help listeners follow along as the student speaks.
A single photo of a total eclipse shows only one stage and misses the before-and-after change.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this poem:

'The old oak tree in our yard
has four kinds of visitors:
crows in the high branches,
squirrels in the middle,
a robin's nest just below that,
and a hollow at the bottom
where a raccoon sleeps.'

What type of visual would help a listener understand and feel this poem? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a drawing of the oak tree divided into four labeled zones from top to bottom: crows at the top, squirrels in the middle branches, the robin's nest on a lower branch, and the raccoon's hollow at the base. Each animal should be illustrated in its zone. This visual perfectly matches the poem's structure, which is organized from top to bottom, and it makes the poem feel like a real, living place with each animal in its home.

steps: The poem describes a vertical organization: animals at different heights of the same tree.
A drawing of the tree divided into four labeled zones matches the poem's top-to-bottom structure.
Each zone should show the animal that lives there: crows at top, squirrels mid-section, robin's nest lower, raccoon at bottom hollow.
This visual transforms the poem into a visual 'map' of the tree that the listener can see as they hear the poem.
A photograph of an oak tree alone would show the tree but not the animals in their zones.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about the history of his neighborhood park:

'Our park used to be an empty lot. In 1998, the city planted six oak trees and put in two benches. In 2005, a playground was added. In 2015, the city built a small pond with a fountain. Now people use it every day.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what the visual should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a timeline showing four points from 1998 to today: (1) empty lot, (2) 1998 — oak trees and benches added, (3) 2005 — playground added, (4) 2015 — pond with fountain added. A small icon or drawing beside each date (a tree, a slide, a fountain) would make the changes easy to see. This matches the paragraph's structure, which moves through time, and helps listeners understand how the park grew.

steps: The paragraph describes change over time with specific years.
A timeline is the best visual for a description organized by date.
Four labeled points: empty lot (before 1998), 1998 (trees and benches), 2005 (playground), 2015 (pond).
Small icons beside each date make the additions easy to see at a glance.
A photograph of the current park shows only the end state, not the history.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph describing a book character:

'In my book, the main character Zora is a ten-year-old girl with short natural hair and round glasses. She always carries a worn purple backpack and a notebook with a lightning bolt on the cover. She speaks quietly, but when she has an important idea, her voice gets loud and her hands move fast.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a character illustration of Zora drawn by the student: short natural hair, round glasses, the worn purple backpack on her back, and the lightning-bolt notebook in one hand. An optional second sketch could show her speaking with hands moving, to capture the personality detail. This helps listeners see the character clearly and connects the visual details in the paragraph to a real picture.

steps: The paragraph describes a character's physical appearance and a key personality behavior.
A character illustration shows short hair, glasses, purple backpack, and lightning-bolt notebook.
A second sketch of Zora speaking with hands moving could capture the personality element.
Character illustrations are especially useful for book descriptions because the character only exists in the reader's imagination.
A photograph of a real person would be someone different; a student-drawn illustration is the right choice.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph describing a family tradition:

'Every winter solstice, my family makes a giant paper lantern together. We each paint one panel of the lantern with something we are grateful for from the past year. Then we light a candle inside and carry it through our neighborhood at night. When we get home, we write our wishes for the next year on small pieces of paper and tuck them into the lantern.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a photograph or drawing of the actual lantern the family made, showing the painted panels with gratitude images. A second image could show the family carrying the glowing lantern at night. Together, these would show both the artwork on the lantern and the tradition of carrying it — two distinct and meaningful parts of the description. If only one visual is possible, a close-up of the painted lantern panels is the most unique and specific part of the tradition.

steps: The paragraph describes two distinct visual moments: the painted lantern and the carrying at night.
A photograph or drawing of the lantern's panels shows the art-making tradition and what it looks like.
A photograph of the family carrying the glowing lantern at night shows the second tradition.
If one visual, the painted panels are the most unique part — the painted gratitude images make this tradition specific.
A photograph of a store-bought lantern would not show the personal, hand-painted nature of this tradition.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about how eyeglasses work:

'People who are nearsighted can see things up close but not far away. Their eyes focus light in front of the retina instead of on it. Eyeglass lenses bend the light before it enters the eye so that it lands on the retina. This makes far-away things look clear.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a side-by-side diagram showing two cross-sections of an eye: one without glasses (light landing in front of the retina, causing blur) and one with glasses (lens bending the light so it lands on the retina, causing clarity). Arrows should show the path of light in each case. This makes the invisible process of light bending visible and directly matches the cause-and-effect explanation in the paragraph.

steps: The paragraph describes an invisible process: where light lands in the eye and how glasses fix it.
A side-by-side diagram shows the problem (light in front of retina) and the solution (glasses bending light to retina).
Arrows showing the path of light make the bending process visible.
Labels like 'retina,' 'lens,' 'light path' connect to the words in the description.
A photograph of eyeglasses shows only the object, not how they work inside the eye.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about the food chain in a pond:

'In a pond, algae use sunlight to grow. Small insects eat the algae. Small fish eat the insects. Larger fish eat the small fish. Herons and egrets eat the larger fish. Each living thing depends on the one below it in the chain.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a vertical food chain diagram showing five levels from bottom to top: algae at the bottom, insects above it, small fish above that, larger fish next, and heron or egret at the top. Arrows pointing upward from each organism to the next should be labeled 'eats.' This directly matches the paragraph's structure, which describes a bottom-to-top chain of eating, and makes the relationships between organisms clear at a glance.

steps: The paragraph describes a food chain with five levels in a specific order.
A vertical diagram from bottom (algae) to top (heron) with upward arrows labeled 'eats' matches the structure.
Each level should show an illustration or image of the organism.
The upward arrows show direction of energy flow and which organism eats which.
A photograph of a pond shows the habitat but not the relationships described.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph recounting a memory of being sick:

'When I was in kindergarten I had the flu for a whole week. My mom set up a sick station on the couch: blanket, three pillows, the remote control, a glass of water, and my stuffed elephant named Gray. She brought me soup twice a day. I remember the soup bowl had sunflowers on it.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a drawing of the 'sick station' on the couch: the three pillows stacked up, a blanket, the remote control, the glass of water, and the stuffed elephant Gray. The sunflower soup bowl could be shown nearby. This visual captures the most specific and personal element of the memory — the carefully prepared space — and brings the listener into the scene. A photograph of a generic sick person on a couch would not show any of the specific, loving details the student described.

steps: The most specific and touching part of the paragraph is the 'sick station' the mom set up.
A drawing of the couch with each item labeled (blanket, pillows, remote, water, Gray the elephant) shows the setup exactly.
Including the sunflower soup bowl honors the specific detail the student remembered.
This visual makes the listener feel the love behind the care.
A generic sick-day photograph would miss all the personal details that make this memory specific.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph about how mountains are formed:

'Some mountains are formed when two plates of Earth's crust push against each other. The pressure slowly pushes the rock upward. Over millions of years, what was flat ground becomes a tall mountain range. The Himalayas were formed this way and are still growing today.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a three-panel diagram showing the process over time: Panel 1 shows two flat plates pushing toward each other with arrows. Panel 2 shows the rock beginning to fold and rise where the plates meet. Panel 3 shows the finished mountain range with the two plates still visible below. Labels should identify the plates and the mountains. This makes a process that takes millions of years and happens underground visible and understandable.

steps: The paragraph describes a slow, invisible process: two plates pushing together, rock rising over millions of years.
A three-panel sequence diagram shows before, during, and after.
Panel 1: flat plates with arrows pointing toward each other.
Panel 2: plates meeting, rock beginning to buckle and rise.
Panel 3: completed mountain range with plates still visible underground.
Labels connect the visual to the vocabulary in the description.

items.prompt:
A student wrote this paragraph recounting a favorite family recipe:

'My family's tamale recipe has been passed down for four generations. My great-great-grandmother brought it from Oaxaca, Mexico. My great-grandmother changed the chile blend. My grandmother added a corn and cheese filling. My mom makes them every December and teaches me a little more each year.'

What type of visual would help the listener most? Explain specifically what it should show.
items.answer: The best visual would be a family tree or timeline diagram showing the four generations: great-great-grandmother at the top (with a note: 'brought from Oaxaca'), great-grandmother below (note: 'changed the chile blend'), grandmother next (note: 'added corn and cheese filling'), and mom at the bottom (note: 'teaches the recipe every December'). This visual shows how the recipe was passed down and changed, turning a family history into something a listener can see at a glance.

steps: The paragraph describes a recipe passed through four generations, with each person adding something.
A vertical family tree or generational timeline shows the line of passing-down clearly.
Each generation should be labeled with the person's role and what they contributed to the recipe.
Starting at the top (oldest) and moving down to the present matches how family histories are typically shown.
A photograph of tamales shows the food but not the four-generation history that makes this story meaningful.
